3700:
** ὀπτάζομαι**,
_passive_, **to be seen,** {{LXX|LXX.Num.14.14}}:—so **ὀπτάνομαι**,{{LXX+5th c.BC+|LXX.3Ki.8.8, “UPZ” 62.32 (2nd c.BC), “PTeb.” 24.5 (2nd c.BC), NT.Act.1.3, [3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristophanes Byzantinus Philosophus] argument 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 4, “PMag.Par.” 1.3033, “Corpus Hermeticum” 3.2}}:—an _active_ **ὀπταίνω** in {{Refs|12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 069.33.}}
3701:
** ὀπτᾰσία**, ἡ
**A**, (ὀπτάζομαι) **vision,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|Anthologia Graeca 6.210 codices (4th-3rd c.BC: Philetas}}; see at {ὁπλισία}), {{LXX+NT|LXX.Est.4.17, NT.Luke.1.22}}; simply, **appearance,** {{LXX|LXX.Mal.3.2, LXX.Sir.43.2.}}
3707:
** ὁρ-ᾱτός**, ή, όν,
**to be seen, visible,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “παραγγελίαι” 14: joined with ἁπτός, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 28b, +others}}; opposed to νοητός, {{Refs|[prev. author] “R.” 509d, 524c, etc.}}; compare ὁρατικός. _adverb_ **-τῶς**{{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 23.4, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1029e.}}
3711:
** ὀργ-ίλος** [ῐ], η, ον,
(ὀργή II) **inclined to anger, irascible,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.19, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 9.7, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.33, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1108a7}}: _comparative_ **-ώτερος**[{{Refs 1st c.BC+|[prev. author] “Cat.” 10a7, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.74 W., 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 15.7.4 (variant{-αίτερος})}}]. _adverb_ -λως, ἔχειν **to be angry,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.215}}; τινι with one, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|[prev. author] 45.67; ἐπί τινι 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 8.25.6; διατίθεσθαι 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.42}} W.: _neuter_ as _adverb_, ὀργίλον βλέπειν {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 3.103b, 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 62.24}}: _comparative_ **-ώτερον**{{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 3.2.3.}}
3718:
** ὀρθο-τομέω**,
**cut in a straight line,** τὰς ὁδούς {{LXX|LXX.Pro.3.6: _metaphorically_, ὀ. τὸν λόγον}} **teach** it **aright,** {{NT|NT.2Tim.2.15.}}
3720:
** ὀρθρ-ινός**, ή, όν,
(ὄρθρος) later form {{LXX+5th c.BC+|(2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista “Praeparatio Sophistica” p.93 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus) for ὄρθριος, LXX.Wis.11.22, +others}}; ὀρθρινὸς οἴχεσθαι {{Refs 1st c.BC+|“Anthologia Graeca” 5.176 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus); ὀ. δῶρα [prev. work] 7.195 ([prev. author]): _neuter_ _plural_ as}} _adverb_, ὀρθρινὰ παίζειν{{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. work] 12.47 ([prev. author]). [ῐ “Anthologia Graeca” 5.176, 12.47, as in ἠρινός, θερινός, χειμερινός: 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 948, “Anthologia Graeca” 6.160 (Antip. Sid.)}}, etc. make ι long, probably in imitation of ὀπωρῑνῷ which is a metrically necessity in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, see entry]}}
3726:
** ὁρκ-ίζω**,
_Doric dialect_ _future_ ὁρκιξέω {{Refs 4th c.BC+|“IG” 22.1126.13 (Delph.):—like ὁρκόω (used with it in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.278)}}, **make** one **swear, administer an oath to** a person, τιν; rejected by {{Refs 5th c.BC+|2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 338, but found in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.10, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.30, 19.278, 23.172, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 149, “PCair.Zen.” 254.2 (3rd c.BC)}}; ὁ. ἐφ᾽ ᾧ ἔσται {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|“SIG” 684.25 (Dyme, 2nd c.BC)}}: with _double_ _accusative_, ὁ. τινὰς ὅρκον {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|“IG” 9(2).1109.52 (Thess., 2nd-1st c.BC), 5(1).1390.1 (Andania, 1st c.BC)}}; ὁ. τινά, with _infinitive_, {{LXX|LXX.Neh.5.12}}; **adjure,** δαίμονας, with _infinitive_, {{LXX+NT+5th c.AD+|“PMag.Par.” 1.345; ὁ. τινὰ κατὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ LXX.2Ch.36.13, compare “PMag.Par.” 1.289, “PMag.Lond.” 121.242; ὁρκίζω σε τὸν Θεόν NT.Mark.5.7, compare “PMag.Par.” 1.3045; οὐρανὸν ὁρκίζω σε 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Fragmenta” 299; ὁ. σε τοῖς Μήδων καὶ Περσῶν δόγμασιν ἵνα.. LXX.Dan.6.13}}:—_passive_, **to be sworn,** ὡρκισμένοι νόμῳ ἰητρικῷ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Jusj.”, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 38.13.5.}}
3728:
** ὁρκ-ωμοσία**, ἡ,
**swearing, oath,** {{LXX+NT+2nd c.AD+|LXX.Eze.17.18, NT.Heb.7.20, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1. 38.}}
3740:
** ὁσάκις** [ᾰ],
_Epic dialect_ **ὁσσάκι**, as always in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus}}; also **ὁσσάκις**, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“Tab.Heracl.” 1.132, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 2.2}}: (ὅσος):— **as many times as, as of ten as,** Relat. to τοσσάκι, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.265, 22.194, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.585}}; _Attic dialect_ form in {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.18, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 143a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.4.3, NT.1Cor.11.25, etc.}}:—also **ὁσᾰκισδήποτε**, {{Refs|Dosith. p.409}} K.; **ὁσᾰκισοῦν**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Nicomachus Gerasenus Mathematicus “Arithmetica Introductio” 2.17.}}
3742:
** ὁσι-ότης**, ητος, ἡ,
**disposition to observe divine law, piety,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 329c, “Euthphr.” 14df, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.47, “SIG” 654 B 10 (Delph., 2nd c.BC), etc.}}; πρὸς θεῶν ὁ. **piety towards** them, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 34; πρὸς τοὺς θεούς [prev. author] 2.359f}}; also, like Latin _pietas,_ ἡ πρὸς γονεῖς ὁ. {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 7.4; πρὸς τὴν τεκοῦσαν [prev. author] 31.27.}}
3757:
** οὗ**,
_genitive_ of _relative_ and possess. Prons. ὅς: as _adverb_ **where**, see at {ὅς}, ἥ, ὅ A b. 1.
3758:
** οὐά**
or **οὐᾶ**, Latin _vah!_ exclamation of admiration, or of astonishment, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.22.34, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 63.20}}; of irony, {{NT|NT.Mark.15.29.}}
3760:
** οὐδᾰμ-ῶς**,
_adverb_ of οὐδαμός, **in no wise**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.148, 173}}; ἄλλως οὐ. {{Refs|[prev. author] 1.123, etc.}}; οὐδέποτε οὐδαμῇ οὐ. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 78d, compare “Phlb.” 29b}}: frequently in answers, πότερα γὰρ.. πρέπε;—οὐ. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 240, compare 716; so οὐ. γ᾽ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 688, “V.” 79, etc.}}; also **οὐθαμῶς**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Metaphysica” 7, etc.}} —Cf. μηδαμῶς.
3763:
** οὐδέποτε**,
in _Ionic dialect_ Prose **οὐδέκοτε**, _Doric dialect_ **οὐδέποκα** probably in {{Refs|“IG” 22.1126.5 (compare μηδέποκα [prev. work] 11)}}, etc.:—_conjunction_ and _adverb_ **and not ever** or **nor ever, not even ever** or **never**, in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus}} mostly with past tenses, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.155, 5.789, +others}}: but with _present_, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.464, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 759}}: with _future_, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.203, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 176}}; in _Attic dialect_, οὐδέποτε is commonly found with _present_ or _future_ (or its equivalent, as in οὐδέποτε μὴ λειφθῇ {{Refs 1st c.AD+|“SIG” 800.29 (Lycosura, 1st c.AD)), οὐδεπώποτε}} with past tenses, so οὐδέποτε ἐπὶ μέλλοντος.., ἐπὶ δὲ παρῳχημένου τὸ οὐδεπώποτε {{Refs 5th c.BC+|2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista “Praeparatio Sophistica” p.91 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus: but οὐδέποτε}} occurs with past tenses in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“Comica Adespota” 23 (cited by 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista [same place]), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.13, “Ages.” 11.7, “Oec.” 20.22, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.151, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 653}}; compare οὐδέποτε **tam in praeterito quam in futuro, quomodo et nos 'nunquam'**, {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th-6th c.AD: Priscianus Grammaticus “Inst.” 18.257}}: in late writers the reference of πω to past time was neglected, see at {οὐδεπώποτε}, and{{Refs 1st c.AD+|compare ἐξ ὧν ἀνάγκη.. μηδεπώποτε ἐλευθερίας ἐπιτυγχάνειν 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 14.1}}; compare οὐδέπω, οὔποτε, οὔπω, οὐπώποτε, also μηδέποτε, μηπώποτε.—In {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus οὐδέ ποτε}} should probably be written divisim: sometimes a word is put between, as in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.99.}}
3764:
** οὐδέ πω**,
_conjunction_ and _adverb_ **and not yet, not as yet**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 322, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 172c, etc.: in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, mostly with a word between, οὐδέ τί πω, οὐδ᾽ ἄν πω, etc., always of the past (compare οὔπω)}}: later with _present_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 106b, etc.; σὺ δὲ οὐδέπω ὁρᾷς 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 21}}: with _future_, ὅσον οὐδέπω συμβήσεσθαι {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Zosimus Epigrammaticus 2.1}}; compare οὐδέποτε.
3765:
** οὐκέτι**
or **οὐκ ἔτι,** _adverb_ **no more, no longer, no further**: and generally, **not now**, opposed to οὔπω (not yet), frequently in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus}}, and _Attic dialect_; οὐκέτι πάμπαν {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.701; οὐκέτι πάγχυ 19.343}}; with a word between, οὐ πάμπαν ἔτι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|13.7; οὐ γὰρ ἔτι 2.13, 141, etc.—Sts. reversely, ἔτ᾽ οὐκ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 161, compare ἔτ᾽ οὐδέν [prev. author] “Ph.” 1217 (Lyric poetry); ἔτ᾽ οὐδείς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1177.}}
3771:
** οὐρᾰνό-θεν**
(_paroxytone_), _adverb_ **from heaven, down from heaven**, {{LXX+8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.294, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 761, LXX.4Mac.4.10, “JRS” 17.49 (Phrygia, 4th c.AD)}}: joined with Preps., ἀπ᾽ οὐ. {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.199, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.18, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 384}}; ἐξ οὐ. {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.19, 21, 17.548}}; κατ᾽ οὐ. {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Lithica” 601.}}
3773:
**Οὐρβανός**, -οῦ, ὁ (Lat. Urbanus),
**Urban**: Rom.16:9.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
3774:
**Οὐρίας**, -ου, ὁ (Heb. אוּרִיָּה),
**Uriah**: Mat.1:6.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
3781:
** ὀφειλ-έτης**, ου, ὁ,
**debtor**, τινι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 736d, etc.}}; ὀ. εἰμί with _infinitive_, I am **under bond** to.., {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 590, cf. NT.Rom.8.12}}: —_feminine_ **ὀφειλ-έτις**, ιδος, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 965.}}
3783:
** ὀφείλ-ημα**, ατος, τό,
**that which is owed, debt**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40, etc.}}; ἀποτίνειν ὀ. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 717b; ἀποδοτέον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1165a3: also in Inscrr., “IG” 12.57.14, “SIG” 306.38 (Tegea, 4th c.BC), 1108.11 (Callatis, 3rd-2nd c.BC), etc.}}; and Papyrus, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PHib.” 1.42.10 (3rd c.BC), etc.}}; compare ὀφήλωμα.
3794:
** ὀχῠρ-ωμα**, ατος, τό,
**stronghold, fortress, prison**, {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.3, LXX.Gen.39.20, “PPetr.” 2p.34 (3rd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.6.3, “PStrassb.” 85.23 (2nd c.BC): _plural_, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.334 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, “OGI” 455.14 (Aphrodisias, 1st c.BC).}}
3795:
** ὀψ-άριον**, τό,
_diminutive_ of ὄψον, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 45, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 95, 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 27, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 32, “Test.Epict.” 6.11, “PPetr.” 3p.327 (3rd c.BC), “PCair.Zen.” 440.3 (3rd c.BC), etc.}}; λαγύνιον ταριχηροῦ (i.e. -ῶν) ὀψαρίων a jar of pickled **fish**, {{NT+1st c.AD+|“BGU” 1095.17 (1st c.AD),compare “PRyl.” 229.21 (1st c.AD), NT.John.6.9, +others, “OGI” 484.12 (Pergam., 2nd c.AD).}}
3797:
** ὄψῐμος**, ον,
(ὀψέ) _poetry_ for ὄψιος, **late, slow**, τέρας ὄ. **for** (concerned with) **a late time**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.325}}: in Prose, **late in the season**, σπόρος [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 17.4, 5, but _falsa lectio_ for{ὄψιος} in 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.9.7, +others}}]; of crops, {{LXX+3rd c.BC+|LXX.Exo.9.32, “PSI” 4.433.2 (3rd c.BC), “PCair.Zen.” 299.2 (3rd c.BC)}}; ἐν τοῖς ὀ. τῶν ὑδάτων {{NT+1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.10; ὑετὸς πρώϊμος καὶ ὄ. NT.Jam.5.7}}: _comparative_, καιρὸς -ώτερος {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|“PFay.” 133.9 (3rd c.AD)}}; **recent**, ποιητική {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.674f}}. _adverb_ **-μως**{{Refs 8th c.BC+|“PTeb.” 72.361 (2nd c.BC), “POxy.” 474.24 (2nd c.AD), 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus ad 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 483.}}
3798:
** ὀψία**,
_Ionic dialect_ -ιη (i.e. ὥρα), ἡ, **the latter part of day, evening**, opposed to ὄρθρος, frequently joined with δείλη (which see), μέχρι δείλης ὀψίης {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.167; περὶ δείλην ὀ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.26}}; δείλης ὀ. **late** in the evening, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.9}}; ὀψίας alone, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|“POxy.” 528.5 (2nd c.AD).}} —Cf. ὄψιος.
